scenes.say: Would you hurt a stranger, just because someone told you to?
scenes.cap: Would you HURT a stranger, just because someone TOLD you to?

scenes.say: In nineteen sixty-one, Yale psychologist Stanley Milgram tested ordinary people.
scenes.cap: In 1961, Yale psychologist STANLEY MILGRAM tested ordinary people.

scenes.say: You are the teacher. For every wrong answer, you shock the learner.
scenes.cap: You are the TEACHER. For every wrong answer, you SHOCK the learner.

scenes.say: Fifteen volts. Then thirty. Then more.
He screams. He begs you to stop. Then he goes silent.
scenes.cap: He SCREAMS. He begs you to STOP. Then he goes SILENT.

scenes.say: A man in a grey lab coat says, please continue.
scenes.cap: A man in a grey lab coat says: PLEASE CONTINUE.

scenes.say: In the first study, how many went all the way, to four hundred and fifty volts?
scenes.cap: In the first study, how many went ALL THE WAY, to 450 VOLTS?

scenes.say: The shocks were fake. The learner was an actor.
scenes.cap: The shocks were FAKE. The learner was an ACTOR.

scenes.say: But the people pressing the buttons did not know that.
scenes.cap: But the people pressing the buttons DID NOT KNOW that.

upload.title: Would You Obey? 65% Did ⚡ #shorts
upload.description:
In 1961 at Yale, psychologist Stanley Milgram asked ordinary people to give electric shocks to a 'learner' whenever he got an answer wrong. In his first study, 65% went all the way to 450 volts when a man in a lab coat told them to continue. The shocks were fake and the learner was an actor.

Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milgram_experiment
